title: improv·artist · naïve (Henri Rousseau)
mutation_directive: improv artist: naïve via Henri Rousseau

improv_extras.practice: untrained jungle paintings; flat foliage, fixed gaze, dreamlike clarity

v1.feedback: The Rousseau idea lands — Lucy as a statue glimpsed through layered flat foliage is a legit reading of the brief, and the graduated green palette with rare bloom accents is restrained and period-appropriate. Two issues: the foliage is distributed as a uniform cylinder of ellipses, which reads more like a particle cloud than Rousseau's characteristic overlapping flat leaf planes with hard silhouette edges — try planar quads or orient clusters into distinct frontal layers with depth-sorted alpha to get that stage-flat cutout look. The camera is fixed at z=32 which frames Lucy well but wastes the horizontal thirds; a slight off-center shift and tighter FOV would better evoke Rousseau's cramped, airless compositions where foliage presses against every edge.

v2.feedback: The Rousseau idea lands partially — flat foliage quads in discrete depth layers with a restrained green palette is the right instinct, and the rare yellow bloom accents are a nice touch. But the Lucy statue as centerpiece fights the brief: Rousseau painted jungles with animals and figures embedded in foliage, not classical sculptures. The foliage reads more as confetti rectangles than Rousseau's dense, overlapping, meticulously outlined leaves — try elongated rounded shapes with visible vein lines or layered opacity to get that flat-but-lush tapestry feel. The camera is static and distant; pulling in tighter and letting the leaves occlude the figure more (80% hidden, eyes peeking through) would channel Rousseau's dreamlike fixed-gaze compositions far better than a fully visible statue with sparse leaf scatter.
